item.title: Carrick shrugs off Man Utd sack talk ahead of Roma match
item.description: Michael Carrick brushed off suggestions he has just two games left as Manchester United boss as he prepares his underperforming side for Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Roma. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford is increasingly precarious following Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, which extended United’s winless run in all competitions to nine games — they last had a longer such sequence in 1984. Former United and England midfielder Carrick was asked at his pre-match press conference on Monday whether he felt he had just two games remaining at the helm — against Roma and Aston Villa. The Villa match on Sunday comes just before an international break, potentially giving the United hierarchy an opportunity to make a managerial change. “No, not at all,” said the 45-year-old, in his first full season in charge. “If you look into the future, you never know what’s going to happen. “I don’t know what’s going to happen. That doesn’t change the way I feel, how we’re preparing for the game tomorrow. “I’m actually really looking forward to the game, can’t wait for the game tomorrow. You might think I’m crazy with the results we’ve had and what’s going on, but I genuinely can’t wait.” Carrick also said he had “no concerns” over the commitment of out-of-form Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez, who was sent off in United’s defeat at Stamford Bridge. The defender had previously criticised club chiefs over a lack of investment in the squad. “Things happen in football, sometimes you do things, sometimes you make decisions, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but the commitment is not an issue for sure,” said Carrick. – Dressing-room mood – The United head coach insisted the dressing room was in “a good place” despite the club’s terrible start to the season. “Perception is a funny thing. You can make things look all sorts of different ways and think about all sorts of different things,” he said. “I’ve said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don’t question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment is not a thing at all.” United are just one place above the Premier League relegation zone after taking a mere seven points from their nine matches so far this season. And they are 20th in the Champions League table following a dismal 4-1 defeat away at Como last month. Only the top 24 teams will progress beyond the league phase. But midfielder Kobbie Mainoo, sitting alongside Carrick at Monday’s press conference, said United could turn things around. “We’ve not had the results we’ve wanted,” said the 21-year-old. “But we need to look forward now. There’s big, big games ahead and I feel like we’re one win away from changing that.” Carrick has fond memories of facing Roma as a member of Alex Ferguson’s team, scoring twice in United’s 7-1 quarter-final second-leg triumph in the Champions League in 2007. “It was a magical night, I have to say,” he recalled

item.title: Miner dies in pit collapse in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — A 35-year-old miner, identified as Ibrahim Jabir, has died following the collapse of a mining pit at Asaradan village in Jos East Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 12:10 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, 2026, trapping the miner in the collapsed pit. A resident of Jos East, Peter Ajik, who confirmed the incident to newsmen in Jos on Monday, said Jabir died at the scene. “The victim, Ibrahim Jabir, died in the incident. The incident happened around 12:10 a.m. when the mining pit collapsed,” Ajik said. He described the incident as another reminder of the dangers associated with mining activities, particularly where adequate safety measures are not observed. Ajik urged miners to take safety precautions seriously and called on relevant authorities to intensify monitoring of mining activities in the area. He also said security operatives responded to a distress call following the collapse. “We are appealing to the relevant authorities to intensify monitoring of mining activities in the area and ensure that safety measures are strictly observed to prevent further loss of lives,” he said. Efforts to reach security operatives for further details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Miner dies in pit collapse in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Democrats, Trump hold final rallies before midterm elections
item.description: Donald Trump and his Republican Party will make last-gasp pitches to US midterm voters Monday to hold back a predicted Democrat wave that could sweep Congress and impose tight political constraints on the president for the first time in two years. For his closing arguments, Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old president’s controversial drive to redevelop the US capital. “We’re going to win,” he said on Sunday. Democrats, meanwhile, prepared a round of final rallies — including by star Democratic Senate candidates James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas — which will cap a campaign of breathtaking tension and bitterness. Polls are largely in their favor, showing that Democrats are poised to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives and have a real shot at winning the currently Republican Senate. Even winning just the House would mean Democrats have voting power over the federal budget and would lead powerful committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues. The loss of total Republican dominance would push Trump into a lame-duck period, with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran, and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington. But a decade into the Trump era, Democrats are wary about predictions of victory. “Nauseously optimistic,” Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood. – Scorched earth – Democrats are also facing late internal divisions, with left-wing candidates clashing at times with the party’s establishment. In a startling display of infighting on Sunday, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens in Michigan endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers against left-wing progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed in her state’s key Senate race. Stevens, who lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite being backed by the Democratic establishment, struggled to explain her decision in an interview with CNN. Trump’s Republicans have fought a political scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and openly branding El-Sayed, who is Muslim, as a terrorist. Addressing a crowd in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said Democrats are “extreme and dangerous radicals” who will “steal your wealth” and let in migrants to “ransack, rape and plunder.” But polls show Americans souring on Trump’s wrecking-ball act. While the House seems highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is up in the air. Only a third of the Senate’s 100 seats are being contested in these midterms, and few of the races were seen as favorable to Democrats. To win the upper chamber, Democrats must flip seats in states the president carried by double digits two years before. This has only happened five times in midterm elections since 1990. item.title: Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,300 people – Africa CDC
item.description: Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the continent’s top health agency. In mid-May, the DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak, a deadly disease transmitted through contact with bodily fluids that causes haemorrhagic fever and has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years. According to data shared with AFP by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) on Monday, the outbreak, which has spread to other countries on the continent, has killed 5,376 people — 5,372 in the DRC and two each in Kenya and Uganda. A total of 10,444 cases have been confirmed, with a fatality rate of more than 50 percent. The virus has crossed borders several times in recent months. Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 cases, almost all involving people who had travelled from the DRC, before being declared Ebola-free in August. In October, Kenya recorded nine infections, marking the first time the country had reported an Ebola case. That same month, Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, reported an Ebola case involving a 42-year-old Swiss woman whose husband works at the Swiss embassy in Abuja. The couple had travelled to Uganda before returning to Nigeria. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which no approved vaccine or treatment is currently available. In recent weeks, clinical trials have begun with the Ervebo vaccine, which has proved effective against the more common Zaire strain of the virus. item.title: We’re facing challenges, hostility around us — Tinubu
item.description: –Says his prayer for wisdom, resilience to continue serving Nigeria has been granted –Reaffirms commitment to Project Nigeria By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has said that although the country is facing challenges and hostility, Nigeria will overcome them through faith in God Almighty. President Tinubu, who is in Mecca for a holy obligation, said he asked for wisdom and resilience to continue serving the people, and that his prayer has been granted, just as it was before the 2023 election, when God answered him. The President made the remarks on Monday while reflecting on his spiritual journey to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah, during which the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques of Makkah and Madinah, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, granted him the rare privilege of leading Nigeria’s delegation to pray inside the Holy Ka’abah. He reaffirmed his determination to build a prosperous nation, invest in the future of young Nigerians, and pursue development in line with the will of Almighty God and the aspirations of the people. At the Ka’abah, President Tinubu offered prayers of gratitude to Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving as Nigeria’s President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led the President into the Ka’abah. President Tinubu thanked the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his Nigerian delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah and offer prayers to Almighty Allah. The President described the honour as a historic and deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. “I want to say a big thank you for the faith and recognition. I can’t believe the fencing of the Ka’abah is in green, white and green, which reminds us of our Nigerian identity. “I thank the Crown Prince and all the administrators of the Holy Land. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as the leader of the delegation and of the country. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us, but we will overcome them with faith in God Almighty. I am grateful forever. I thank the King and the Crown Prince. “It is an honour that I enjoyed, and it is gracious of them to have allowed me to enter inside the Ka’abah. This is history,” the President said. item.title: Using 1963 Fire Act to fight 2026 fires unacceptable, FG declares
item.description: .Unveils vision of new fire and rescue service .Cuts response time to 15 minutes, 119 lives saved By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has said it makes no sense to continue to rely on a fire law enacted in 1963 to tackle fire emergencies in 2026, as it prepares to send a new Federal Fire and Rescue Service Act to President Bola Tinubu soon for assent. Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said this on Monday in Abuja at the opening ceremony and stakeholders’ conference of the 2026 National Fire Safety Week. “You cannot have a Federal Fire Service Act of 1963, and you think it would be 2026-compliant. It doesn’t make sense” the minister said. He said the old law denies firefighters the powers they need to do their work. “If the law does not give you the power to do something, no matter how good that action is, once you do it, it becomes illegal. There is no right way of doing something that is legally wrong,” he said. Tunji-Ojo said the review of the Act had been completed and the new bill should be laid before the President in a matter of days. He said it was the first time in 63 years that any government had taken up the task. The minister said the new law would open the sector to private sector intervention and move the service beyond firefighting. “When it comes to hazards, fire is only one of the hazards. Even flood, water can be hazardous,” he said. He said he wanted a Federal Fire Service that responds to medical emergencies, floods, chemical spills, toxic materials, bomb attacks and earthquakes. He added that fire suppression was only one of about twenty responsibilities of fire services elsewhere. “I want to see a Federal Fire Service whose specialisation is rescue operations,” he said. Tunji-Ojo also called for stronger fire inspection and code enforcement, with volunteer fire marshals in every district and town. He said the service should work with education authorities to make rescue skills part of school curricula. “If anything happens, maybe somebody faints, what percentage of Nigerians can even do a simple resuscitation process?” he asked. The minister said the service should also investigate emergencies beyond fire incidents, and should chair a council of fire and rescue services to coordinate policy across the country. On performance, the minister said the average response time to fire incidents was between 32 and 35 minutes when the administration came into office. He said it now stands at 15 minutes, 22 seconds. He said that as of August, 119 lives were saved with no life lost to fire in 36 incidents nationwide. “There is a lot he’s working under the old law, so there’s a limit to how well he can do this,” Tunji-Ojo said of the Controller-General of the Federal Fire Service, Olumode Samuel Adeyemi. The minister said the National Fire Academy was 85 per cent complete and would be running by the end of the year, with commissioning expected in December. item.title: 2027: Give Tinubu, Otu another term, Shettima tells Cross River
item.description: …says authority belongs to the people …Bakassi Deep seaport will be one Nigeria’s maritime gateway By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR Nigeria’s vice president, Senator Kashim Shettima, on Monday, held out the promise of a deep seaport in Bakassi and the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway to Cross River voters, asking them to renew the mandate of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Bassey Otu in 2027. Representing the President at the APC Presidential Campaign rally at the U.J. Esuene Stadium, Shettima brought the President’s greetings and thanked the people for standing by the administration. “Over the past three years, you have shown us support, and you have resisted the lies and propaganda intended to misrepresent us,” he said. He described the relationship with the people of Cross River and Nogeria at large as “an alliance of prosperity, an alliance of opportunity”. He said the APC was seeking votes for Tinubu, Governor Otu, and candidates for the National Assembly and the State House of Assembly. “We are asking because authority belongs to the people. Those entrusted with authority must return with an account of their stewardship.” Turning to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, he said the project would “connect coastal communities” and “ease the movement of goods and people.” He added that it would expand tourism, attract investors and create thousands of direct and indirect jobs. On the Bakassi Deep Seaport, he said the project had received federal government approval. “When completed, it will become an international maritime gateway. It will attract shipping companies. It will generate employment,” he said. He said the two projects were part of a plan to make Cross River a major beneficiary of the government’s maritime economy agenda. The vice president also spoke about education, saying the government’s student financing intervention would drive human capital development in the state. He said it would give relief to parents and widen access to higher education so that no parent would be forced to abandon a child’s schooling for lack of funds. Shettima praised the party faithful at the rally, saying they were “chosen by you, endorsed by you.” He asked them to vote for the APC “from top to bottom” in the 2027 elections. “You, the people, are the purpose and authority of you,” he declared. item.title: 2027: Critics of Rainbow Coalition incapable of uniting their own families – Wike
item.description: …Tells FCT residents, ‘election day is not for market or fishing’ By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said politicians who deny the existence of the Rainbow Coalition lack the capacity to unite even their own families and communities. Wike spoke on Monday in Abuja at the commissioning of the Gwagwalada Civic Centre and an interactive session with stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress APC and the Peoples Democratic Party PDP in Gwagwalada Area Council. The minister said the coalition, which brings together political stakeholders from both parties, was formed in the interest of unity, cooperation and development in the FCT. “Some greedy and selfish politicians do not understand what we call unity. They have no capacity to hold their space, they have no capacity to even hold their families, and they have no capacity to hold their communities. So they can open their mouths and say there is no Rainbow Coalition,” he said. Wike challenged critics of the alliance to explain why political leaders who once disagreed could not come together to pursue common interests. He described the development in Gwagwalada as a departure from the politics of confrontation, insisting that the FCT needed cooperation rather than needless political hostility. Commending political leaders in the area for setting aside their differences, he said their decision showed that the collective interest of the people outweighed individual political ambition. Wike also urged residents not to repeat what he described as the mistake of the 2023 general elections and called for credible representation at the National Assembly. The minister canvassed support for a former senator, Philip Aduda, and other candidates endorsed by the coalition, saying political representatives must be accessible and familiar with their constituents. Wike also declared support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and urged residents to turn their endorsements into votes in 2027. “On the day of the election, it will not be a day for market or fishing. It is the day all of us have decided to come together and demonstrate our strength through our votes. Go to the polling units, districts and communities and mobilise the people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Earlier, the FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Tanko Yamawo, described the gathering as historic, saying Wike’s intervention had brought together leaders who previously operated on opposing sides. The FCT PDP Chairman, Alhaji Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, praised Wike for his development interventions, particularly the revival of a project abandoned for 16 years in Gwagwalada. The Aguma of Gwagwalada, Alhaji Muhammadu Magaji, also commended Wike’s contributions to the development of the territory. He said the revival of the abandoned project underscored the importance of continuity in governance. item.title: 2027: Obi couldn’t fix Anambra; Atiku will return to Dubai after election — Oshiomhole
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Senator Adams Oshiomhole has criticised former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, questioning their capacity to lead Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Oshiomhole said Obi failed to address Anambra State’s challenges during his eight years as governor, while predicting that Atiku would return to Dubai after losing the presidential election. The former Edo State governor made the remarks during an All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally in Cross River State, where he urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Questioning Obi’s promise to govern Nigeria for only four years, Oshiomhole said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDCa) had not demonstrated the capacity to deliver within that period. “If Peter Obi could not fix Anambra State in eight years, how can he look you korokoro in the eye and say he will do it in four years?” he asked. He also took a swipe at Atiku, accusing the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of spending much of his time outside the country and returning to Nigeria during election periods. “Atiku, who lives in Dubai, only comes home at the eve of every election. When he loses this one, as he will lose, in January or by February, Atiku will be back in Dubai,” he said. Oshiomhole, however, used the campaign to highlight what he described as the achievements of the Tinubu administration, particularly in Cross River State. He said the state’s recognition as an oil-producing state following the resolution of its non-littoral status would increase revenue accruing to the state and improve its economic prospects. On education, the senator said the Federal Government’s student loan scheme had provided opportunities for young people whose parents could not afford their school fees. He described Tinubu as a leader who prioritises access to education, arguing that students should not be denied opportunities because of their parents’ financial circumstances. Oshiomhole also pointed to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Road project, saying its completion would bring economic opportunities and development to Cross River State. The senator also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic policies, particularly the abolition of multiple exchange rates. He argued that the previous system created different exchange rates for people based on their connections, adding that the current arrangement had established a uniform exchange rate across the country. According to Oshiomhole, implementing the policies required courage and visionary leadership. He urged Cross River residents to reject the opposition parties, insisting that the APC had established a strong political presence in the state. “Today, tomorrow, and forever, I believe APC has come to stay in Cross River, and together we will advance the growth and development of Nigeria,” he said. item.title: 2027: Accord Party challenges suit seeking to disqualify all its candidates
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Accord Party (AP) has approached the Federal High Court in Abuja for the dismissal of a suit seeking to disqualify all its candidates for the 2027 general elections. The party, in a preliminary objection filed through a team of lawyers led by a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Mr. Musibau Adetunbi, maintained that the court lacks the jurisdiction to entertain the legal action filed by its National Secretary, Mr. Adebukola Ajaja. It argued that the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CV/2524/2026, lacked competence as it was filed outside the 14-day period allowed by law. Insisting that the action had become statute-barred, the party further contended that the issue bordered on the nomination of candidates, which it said falls within the domestic affairs of a political party and is non-justiciable. Moreover, while querying the locus standi (legal right) of the plaintiff to file the action, Accord Party noted that he is not an aspirant in the primary election it conducted on May 29. It also faulted the competence of the suit on the ground that proper parties were not included. The Accord Party argued that while the plaintiff wants the court to nullify the nomination of its candidates, none of the candidates who would be affected by the outcome of the suit were made parties, to afford them the opportunity of being heard. The party further described the suit as “premature”, arguing that the plaintiff failed to give the required 21 days’ pre-action notice. It told the court that its primary was conducted in accordance with all relevant laws and guidelines, adding that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has since recognised its outcome and the list of candidates duly submitted to the electoral umpire in the prescribed format. It further argued that, contrary to the plaintiff’s contention, the National Chairman and the National Organising Secretary could validly sign and submit candidates’ lists and forms to INEC where the National Secretary is unavailable, in line with Article 18 of the party’s constitution and Regulations 25(3) and 28(2) of INEC’s Guidelines. Accord Party added: “INEC Regulations and Guidelines for Political Parties did not in any way specify that the plaintiff herein must sign the forwarding letter, neither did the Constitution of the second defendant require her (the plaintiff) to sign. “The National Executives of the party expressly authorized the fourth defendant to co-sign with the 3rd Defendant. No wrong has been done.” Relying on the Supreme Court’s decision in Jegede v. INEC, Accord Party argued that even if only its National Chairman had signed, “the plaintiff’s case is still bound to fail because the signature of the National Chairman suffices on the authority of Jegede v. item.title: Two killed, five injured in Plateau attacks
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Two persons have been killed while five others sustained injuries in separate attacks on Toul and Halle communities in Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State. The attacks reportedly occurred at about 9pm on Sunday, November 1, 2026, when gunmen opened fire on residents in the two communities. A Mangu resident, Gabriel Titus, who confirmed the incidents to newsmen, said one person was killed and four others injured in the attack on Toul community. Titus said: “The gunmen came into the community and opened fire on the people. “Another person was killed in Halle, while one other person sustained injuries during the attack.” He lamented that the attacks occurred despite a curfew imposed by the state government to prevent further violence in the area. “There is a curfew in place, but the gunmen still came and carried out the attack,” he said. Titus appealed to security operatives to intensify surveillance and track down those responsible for the attacks. He also called for urgent measures to protect residents of the affected communities, saying the recurring violence had heightened concerns among residents. Efforts to reach security operatives for comments were ongoing as of the time of filing this report. The post Two killed, five injured in Plateau attacks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reps propose 20% cap on trust investments
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has proposed a 20 per cent investment limit on exposure to a single issuer as part of efforts to strengthen the management of trust funds and protect beneficiaries against financial losses. The proposal is contained in the Trustee Investment Bill, 2026 (HB 2762), which seeks to repeal and re-enact the existing Trustee Investments Act of 1957, expand permissible investment opportunities and introduce safeguards against excessive investment risks. Chairman of the House Committee on Capital Market and Institutions, Solomon Bob, disclosed this on Monday at a public hearing on the bill at the National Assembly, Abuja. Bob described the proposed diversification requirement as a critical measure to prevent excessive concentration of trust assets in one investment. He said the existing law was enacted when Nigeria’s financial system was considerably less developed and investment opportunities were limited. According to him, the country’s financial landscape has changed significantly, with the capital market now valued at over N80 trillion, pension assets exceeding N30 trillion and emerging investment opportunities including Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), infrastructure funds and green bonds. “Today, we have a sophisticated capital market worth over N80 trillion, pension assets over N30 trillion, and new asset classes from REITs to Infrastructure Funds to Green Bonds. The world has moved. Our law has not. This hearing is to correct that,” he said. Bob said the proposed legislation was designed to align the legal framework governing trust investments with contemporary financial realities while ensuring that trustees operated within clearly defined investment and accountability standards. Under Clause 3 of the bill, the investment options available to trustees would be expanded to include corporate bonds, equities, collective investment schemes, including Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) and REITs, infrastructure funds, real property, foreign investments through licensed custodians, private equity, regulated virtual assets and environmental, social and governance (ESG)-compliant bonds. He said the expanded investment options would allow trustees to diversify portfolios and potentially improve returns for beneficiaries. However, Bob explained that the proposed 20 per cent limit on investment in a single issuer under Clause 4 was intended to minimise concentration risk and prevent trust portfolios from being excessively exposed to the financial difficulties of one institution. The bill also seeks to strengthen trustees’ fiduciary obligations through Clause 5 by expressly incorporating the principles of loyalty, prudence, care and impartiality. Under the proposed provision, trustees would be required to exercise the level of prudence expected of individuals managing their own financial affairs, while prioritising the interests of beneficiaries. item.title: Ronaldo, Messi, Kane make 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World XI [Full List]
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Harry Kane have been named in the 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World XI, alongside several other leading footballers recognised for their performances during the year. Kane’s nomination comes days after he won the 2026 Ballon d’Or , becoming the first Englishman to claim the prestigious individual award since Michael Owen in 2001. The star-studded selection also features Kylian Mbappe, Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, Lamine Yamal, Pedri, Achraf Hakimi and Thiabut Courtois. The selection considers players’ performances between August 4, 2025, and July 19, 2026, with nominees required to have made at least 30 appearances at domestic top-flight or senior international level. The World XI is determined through votes cast by professional footballers, who select their preferred goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders and forwards, with the final team comprising 11 players. The 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11 will be revealed on Monday, November 9. item.title: Cyberattacks disrupt supermarket fridges across five European countries
item.description: Supermarkets in at least five European countries have been hit by a cyberattack that disrupted refrigeration systems, causing temperatures in some fridges and freezers to rise sharply. The affected countries include Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Luxembourg and Sweden, with several retailers confirming on Monday that their systems had been targeted by hackers. The incident comes about three weeks after a similar cyberattack affected refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets across France, forcing retailers to dispose of spoiled food and raising concerns about food security. No individual or group has claimed responsibility for either attack. In Belgium, Carrefour reported disruptions in about 15 of its 700 stores. The company’s spokesman, Mich Vergauwen, confirmed that the incident was a cyberattack. An Ikea Belgium spokeswoman also said its store in Mons, southwestern Belgium, was affected, with freezer temperatures rising suddenly in the early hours of Monday. Other affected retailers included Delhaize, Colruyt and Intermarche. Delhaize also reported refrigeration problems in four of its stores in Luxembourg. Belgian industrial refrigeration company Sabcobel said it had begun securing its installations following the October 12 attack in France. However, about 10 per cent of the systems had yet to be fixed, including some in stores affected by Monday’s incident. The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Stephan Moelans, told AFP that the impact would have been significantly worse if the security operation had not started earlier. In Sweden, supermarket chain Coop confirmed that six of its approximately 800 stores were affected by a cyber incident on Monday. Its spokesman, Carlos Cancino, said the problem had been resolved and that refrigeration systems were operating normally. He added that the affected stores were connected to a 4G mobile network rather than the updated 5G system, making them more exposed to cyberattacks. The company, however, said it did not know who was responsible. Another Swedish retailer, Ica, reported refrigeration problems in a limited number of stores but said it could not confirm whether they resulted from a cyberattack. Ica spokeswoman Helena Johansson said the affected stores were connected to an external refrigeration control system supplied by Danish manufacturer Danfoss, the same company whose equipment was reportedly involved in the October 12 incident in France. Danfoss had yet to respond to AFP’s request for comment. In Finland, irregular temperatures were detected in some smaller grocery stores operated by the Kesko group. item.title: Tinubu concludes Saudi visit, thanks King Salman for Kaaba access
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has announced the conclusion of his visit to Saudi Arabia, expressing gratitude to King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud for granting him and members of his delegation access to the Holy Kaaba in Makkah. Tinubu disclosed this in a post on his X handle on Monday, describing the opportunity to pray inside Islam’s holiest site as a rare privilege and expressing appreciation for the hospitality extended to the Nigerian delegation. He also thanked Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for the gesture, which he said reflected the longstanding ties of faith and friendship between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. “In those sacred moments, I prayed for peace, unity and prosperity for our dear nation and for all Nigerians,” the President wrote. The visit followed Tinubu’s departure from Abuja on Thursday, October 29, for the Islamic spiritual exercise. The delegation included state governors, Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate; Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu; and Oando Chief Executive Officer, Wale Tinubu. item.title: Six mourners abducted in Benue, N15m ransom demanded
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Six persons, including a man conveying his deceased wife’s corpse from Kano State to Okpoga, headquarters of Okpokwu Local Government Area of Benue State, for burial, have been abducted along Adoka Road in Otukpo Local Government Area. The abductors have reportedly demanded N15 million ransom for the release of the victims. The victims, comprising the bereaved husband and five other mourners accompanying him, were reportedly kidnapped at about 8pm on Friday, while the woman’s corpse was abandoned in their vehicle. A community member, Meddy Olotu, who raised the alarm over the incident, said the victims had remained in captivity since Friday, while efforts to secure their release had yet to yield results as of Monday. According to him, the victims were returning from Kano, where the woman died, and heading to Okpoga for her burial when they were intercepted along Adoka Road. Olotu said: “The man, who is based in Kano, lost his wife, and they were bringing her corpse back home to Okpoga in Okpokwu LGA of Benue State for burial. “They left Kano, and you can imagine the journey from Kano to Benue State. It is a long journey. They got to Adoka at about 8pm. That was the last time the family members could reach them. “That same Friday, around Adoka Road, they were said to have been kidnapped and whisked into the bush, while the corpse of his late wife was left in the vehicle. There were about six of them. “From that Friday till today, Monday, they have not been released. As I speak to you, we learnt the abductors are demanding N15 million ransom.” Describing the incident as particularly distressing, Olotu said the abduction had compounded the grief of the family, which was already mourning the loss of the woman. “For somebody who lost his wife, they kidnapped him and his five friends and left the wife’s corpse on the road. That is terrible,” he said. He said personnel of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) reportedly found the corpse the following morning and took it to the police station at Adoka, from where it was deposited in a mortuary pending the release of the abducted persons. Olotu added that the abductors had maintained contact with the victims’ family, with one of the relatives reportedly able to communicate with them because he understood the language they spoke. “Last night, I spoke with one of the family members who said the people have been calling. Luckily, he understands Hausa, so he is able to communicate with them,” he said. He said the six victims were still being held in the bush as of Monday, while the woman’s corpse remained in a mortuary in Adoka. Olotu appealed to relevant authorities to intensify efforts to rescue the victims, expressing concern that the family might struggle to raise the ransom demanded. item.title: Nigerian teenager convicted for defrauding American man of $800
item.description: The Federal High Court sitting in Ikoyi, Lagos, has convicted and sentenced an 18-year-old man, Hassan Usman Olamilekan, for money laundering involving $800 obtained through a lottery scam. Justice Dipeolu delivered the judgment on October 30, 2026, following Olamilekan’s arraignment by the Lagos Zonal Directorate 1 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Olamilekan was arraigned on a one-count charge of money laundering, contrary to Section 18(2)(a) and punishable under Section 18(3) of the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022. The defendant pleaded guilty to the charge, after which an EFCC operative, Ebuka Abanga, reviewed the facts of the case before the court found him guilty. Justice Dipeolu sentenced him to a fine of N200,000 and ordered him to pay N1 million in restitution to the Federal Government. The court further ordered that he remains in the correctional centre pending payment of the fine and restitution. It also ordered the forfeiture of an iPhone 11 Pro and a Poco C71 mobile phone recovered in connection with the offence. According to the EFCC, investigations revealed that Olamilekan, who claimed to be from the Republic of Benin but was born in Nigeria, operated several social media platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Zangi and iMessage, which he allegedly used for internet fraud. The commission said he met his victim, an American citizen identified as Gary Brewer, through the Zangi application, where he impersonated a white American woman named Julie Leach. Olamilekan reportedly told Brewer that he had won a $250 million lottery prize but needed money to activate the winnings before he could claim the funds. He subsequently persuaded the victim to send him gift cards through the messaging platform. The EFCC said the defendant admitted selling the gift cards through the Cardsonic application, converting the proceeds into naira and transferring the money to his grandmother’s OPay account. He also confessed to benefiting $800 from the fraudulent scheme. Olamilekan was among 21 suspected internet fraudsters arrested by EFCC operatives during a sting operation at Applewood Estate, Orchid Road, Lekki, Lagos State, on October 26, 2026. item.title: Reps move to reform 69-year-old Trustee Investment Act
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has begun moves to reform Nigeria’s 69-year-old Trustee Investments Act, while seeking a coordinated regulatory framework to tackle fraud, fragmented property records and weak consumer protection in the real estate sector. Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, said the proposed reforms were aimed at modernising the country’s legal framework to reflect changing financial and investment realities, while protecting the interests of beneficiaries and investors. Abbas, represented by a member of the House representing Lafia/Obi Federal Constituency, Nasarawa State, Dahiru Abubakar Sarki, spoke on Monday at a public hearing on the Trustee Investment Act (Repeal and Enactment) Bill, 2026, at the National Assembly, Abuja. The bill, sponsored by Solomon Bob, seeks to repeal and replace the existing Trustee Investments Act of 1957, which Abbas described as outdated in the face of developments in Nigeria’s capital market and emerging investment opportunities. He said the existing law was enacted in a substantially different economic and financial environment, noting that the investment landscape had changed considerably over the past seven decades. According to him, capital markets have expanded, financial instruments have become more sophisticated, and new opportunities for investment and wealth creation have emerged, making legislative reform necessary. “The challenge is to strike the right balance between preserving trust assets and enabling reasonable returns on investment. “An excessively restrictive framework may deny beneficiaries legitimate opportunities for growth, while an inadequately regulated one may expose their assets to imprudent decisions and avoidable risks,” he said. Abbas stressed that expanded investment opportunities under the proposed legislation must be accompanied by strong safeguards, clear fiduciary responsibilities, effective risk management and appropriate regulatory oversight. He said trustees must be guided by prudence, integrity and transparency, adding that assets held in trust must be managed in the interests of beneficiaries rather than for the personal advantage of trustees. The Speaker said a credible framework for managing trust investments could contribute to deeper capital markets and more effective mobilisation of domestic resources to support infrastructure development and economic growth. He urged stakeholders to pay particular attention to investment categories, diversification requirements, fiduciary obligations, professional delegation and regulatory oversight in considering the bill. Seeks coordinated real estate regulation In a related development, Abbas has called for a coordinated national real estate regulatory system to tackle property fraud, eliminate institutional overlaps and strengthen investor confidence in Nigeria’s housing market.
